    47→ * @tparam Op The operation type (function object)
    48→ * @tparam Impl The ReactImpl type
    49→ * @tparam U The type of the right-hand side operand
    50→ *

    30→    auto buyPrice = var(100.0).setName("buyPrice"); // Price at which stock was bought
    31→    auto currentPrice = var(105.0);                 // Current market price
    32→
    33→    // === Step 2: Compute profit/loss amount using calc() ===
    34→    // calc() creates a reactive calculation that automatically updates

    36→    auto profit = calc([&]() {

    41→    // expr() creates a reactive expression from operator overloads

    47→    // This will automatically print updates whenever prices change

     8→/**
     9→ * @file basic_example.cpp
    10→ * @brief Basic usage example of the Reaction framework
    11→ *
    12→ * This example demonstrates:
    13→ * - Creating reactive variables with var()
    14→ * - Computing derived values with calc() and expr()
    15→ * - Setting up reactive actions that respond to changes
    16→ * - Basic reactive dataflow patterns
    17→ *
    18→ * Use case: Stock price tracking with automatic profit/loss calculation
    19→ */
    20→
    21→#include <cmath>
    22→#include <iomanip>
    23→#include <iostream>
    24→#include <reaction/reaction.h>
    25→
    26→int main() {
    27→    using namespace reaction;
    28→
    29→    // === Step 1: Create reactive variables for stock prices ===
    30→    auto buyPrice = var(100.0).setName("buyPrice"); // Price at which stock was bought
    31→    auto currentPrice = var(105.0);                 // Current market price
    32→
    33→    // === Step 2: Compute profit/loss amount using calc() ===
    34→    // calc() creates a reactive calculation that automatically updates
    35→    // when its dependencies (buyPrice, currentPrice) change
    36→    auto profit = calc([&]() {
    37→        return currentPrice() - buyPrice();
    38→    });
    39→
    40→    // === Step 3: Compute percentage gain/loss using expr() ===
    41→    // expr() creates a reactive expression from operator overloads
    42→    // This demonstrates the mathematical expression syntax
    43→    auto profitPercent = expr(std::abs(currentPrice - buyPrice) / buyPrice * 100);
    44→
    45→    // === Step 4: Set up reactive logging with action() ===
    46→    // action() creates a side-effect that triggers when dependencies change
    47→    // This will automatically print updates whenever prices change
    48→    auto logger = action([&]() {
    49→        std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(2);
    50→        std::cout << "[Stock Update] Current Price: $" << currentPrice()
    51→                  << ", Profit: $" << profit()
    52→                  << " (" << profitPercent() << "%)\n";
    53→    });
    54→
    55→    // === Step 5: Simulate price changes ===
    56→    // Watch how all dependent calculations update automatically
    57→    currentPrice.value(110.0).value(95.0); // Stock price changes (chained updates)
    58→    buyPrice.value(90.0);                  // Buy price adjusted
    59→
    60→    return 0;
    61→}

1→/*

     8→#pragma once
     9→
    10→#include <memory>
    11→#include <utility>
    12→#include "reaction/core/id_generator.h"
    13→#include "reaction/core/react.h"
    14→#include "reaction/graph/field_graph.h"
    15→#include "reaction/graph/observer_graph.h"
    16→
    17→namespace reaction {
    18→
    19→/**
    20→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive variable (Var) based on VarExpr expression type.
    21→ *
    22→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type held by this reactive variable.
    23→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    24→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    25→ */
    26→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    27→using Var = React<VarExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    28→
    29→/**
    30→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive expression (Expr) based on BinaryOpExpr expression type.
    31→ *
    32→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type produced by this reactive calculation.
    33→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    34→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    35→ */
    36→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    37→using Calc = React<CalcExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    38→
    39→/**
    40→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive action (Action) based on CalcExpr expression type.
    41→ *
    42→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    43→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    44→ */
    45→template <IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    46→using Action = React<CalcExpr, Void, IV, TR>;
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * @brief Base class representing a field container in the reactive graph.
    50→ */
    51→class FieldBase {
    52→public:
    53→    /**
    54→     * @brief Create a reactive field from the provided initial value.
    55→     *
    56→     * This function creates a shared pointer to a ReactImpl representing
    57→     * a variable expression holding the given value. It registers the node
    58→     * to both the global ObserverGraph and FieldGraph using this FieldBase's ID.
    59→     *
    60→     * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    61→     * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    62→     * @tparam T The type of the initial value (deduced).
    63→     * @param t The initial value to store in the field.
    64→     * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR> A reactive wrapper around the stored value.
    65→     */
    66→    template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact T>
    67→    auto field(T &&t) {
    68→        auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<T>(t));
    69→        ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr->shared_from_this());
    70→        FieldGraph::getInstance().addObj(m_id, ptr->shared_from_this());
    71→        return React{ptr};
    72→    }
    73→
    74→    /**
    75→     * @brief Get the unique identifier of this field base.
    76→     *
    77→     * @return uint64_t The unique ID.
    78→     */
    79→    uint64_t getId() {
    80→        return m_id;
    81→    }
    82→
    83→private:
    84→    UniqueID m_id; ///< Unique identifier for this field instance.
    85→};
    86→
    87→/**
    88→ * @brief Create a constant reactive variable wrapping the given value.
    89→ *
    90→ * This is similar to var(), but the wrapped value is const.
    91→ * The reactive node is registered to the ObserverGraph.
    92→ *
    93→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    94→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    95→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
    96→ * @param t The value to wrap as a const reactive variable.
    97→ * @return React<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive constant wrapper.
    98→ */
    99→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   100→auto constVar(SrcType &&t) {
   101→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   102→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   103→    return React{ptr};
   104→}
   105→
   106→/**
   107→ * @brief Create a reactive variable wrapping the given value.
   108→ *
   109→ * If the source type supports the Field concept, binds the field in the FieldGraph.
   110→ * Registers the reactive node to the ObserverGraph.
   111→ *
   112→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   113→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   114→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
   115→ * @param t The value to wrap reactively.
   116→ * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive variable wrapper.
   117→ */
   118→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   119→auto var(SrcType &&t) {
   120→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   121→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   122→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   123→    if constexpr (HasField<SrcType>) {
   124→        FieldGraph::getInstance().bindField(t.getId(), ptr->shared_from_this());
   125→    }
   126→    return React{ptr};
   127→}
   128→
   129→/**
   130→ * @brief Create a reactive expression wrapping the given operator expression.
   131→ *
   132→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph, then sets (evaluates) the expression immediately.
   133→ * Supports both binary and unary operator expressions.
   134→ *
   135→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   136→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   137→ * @tparam OpExpr The operator expression type (binary or unary).
   138→ * @param opExpr The operator expression to wrap.
   139→ * @return React<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   140→ */
   141→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsOpExpr OpExpr>
   142→auto expr(OpExpr &&opExpr) {
   143→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   144→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<OpExpr>(opExpr));
   145→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   146→    ptr->set();
   147→    return React{ptr};
   148→}
   149→
   150→/**
   151→ * @brief Create a reactive calculation based on a callable and its arguments.
   152→ *
   153→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph and immediately sets (evaluates) the calculation.
   154→ *
   155→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   156→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   157→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   158→ * @tparam Args Argument types for the callable.
   159→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   160→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   161→ * @return React<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   162→ */
   163→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   164→auto calc(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   165→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   166→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR>>();
   167→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   168→    ptr->set(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   169→    return React{ptr};
   170→}
   171→
   172→/**
   173→ * @brief Alias for calc(), used to create a reactive action.
   174→ *
   175→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   176→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   177→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   178→ * @tparam Args Argument types.
   179→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   180→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   181→ * @return The reactive action wrapper.
   182→ */
   183→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   184→auto action(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   185→    return calc<TR, IV>(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   186→}
   187→
   188→/**
   189→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive wrapper from a value or expression.
   190→ *
   191→ * If the input is a binary operator expression, creates an expr().
   192→ * If the input is an invocable callable, creates a calc().
   193→ * Otherwise, creates a var().
   194→ *
   195→ * @tparam T The type of input.
   196→ * @param t The input value, expression, or callable.
   197→ * @return Corresponding reactive wrapper.
   198→ */
   199→template <NonReact T>
   200→auto create(T &&t) {
   201→    if constexpr (IsBinaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>) {
   202→        return expr(std::forward<T>(t));
   203→    } else if constexpr (InvocableType<T>) {
   204→        return calc(std::forward<T>(t));
   205→    } else {
   206→        return var(std::forward<T>(t));
   207→    }
   208→}
   209→
   210→/**
   211→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive calculation from a callable and arguments.
   212→ *
   213→ * This function wraps a callable and its arguments into a reactive calculation,
   214→ * which automatically updates when any of its dependencies change.
   215→ *
   216→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   217→ * @tparam Args Argument types to be forwarded to the callable.
   218→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   219→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   220→ * @return A reactive calculation wrapper.
   221→ */
   222→template <typename Fun, typename... Args>
   223→auto create(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   224→    return calc(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   225→}
   226→
   227→/**
   228→ * @brief Begins a batch of reactive updates.
   229→ *
   230→ * This function creates a batch context, deferring propagation of reactive updates
   231→ * until the batch is executed. Useful for grouping multiple changes together efficiently.
   232→ *
   233→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   234→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations.
   235→ * @return A Batch object encapsulating the operation.
   236→ */
   237→template <InvocableType Fun>
   238→auto batch(Fun &&fun) {
   239→    return Batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   240→}
   241→
   242→/**
   243→ * @brief Immediately executes a batch of reactive updates.
   244→ *
   245→ * This function creates a batch context and executes it immediately.
   246→ * Any reactive updates are postponed until the end of the batch execution.
   247→ *
   248→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   249→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations to be executed.
   250→ */
   251→template <InvocableType Fun>
   252→void batchExecute(Fun &&fun) {
   253→    Batch batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   254→    batch.execute();
   255→}
   256→
   257→} // namespace reaction
   258→

    49→ * @brief Base class representing a field container in the reactive graph.

    51→class FieldBase {
    52→public:
    53→    /**
    54→     * @brief Create a reactive field from the provided initial value.
    55→     *
    56→     * This function creates a shared pointer to a ReactImpl representing
    57→     * a variable expression holding the given value. It registers the node
    58→     * to both the global ObserverGraph and FieldGraph using this FieldBase's ID.
    59→     *
    60→     * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    61→     * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    62→     * @tparam T The type of the initial value (deduced).
    63→     * @param t The initial value to store in the field.
    64→     * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR> A reactive wrapper around the stored value.
    65→     */
    66→    template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact T>
    67→    auto field(T &&t) {
    68→        auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<T>(t));
    69→        ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr->shared_from_this());
    70→        FieldGraph::getInstance().addObj(m_id, ptr->shared_from_this());

   112→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   113→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   114→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
   115→ * @param t The value to wrap reactively.
   116→ * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive variable wrapper.
   117→ */
   118→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   119→auto var(SrcType &&t) {

   121→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   122→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);

   125→    }
   126→    return React{ptr};
   127→}

   129→/**
   130→ * @brief Create a reactive expression wrapping the given operator expression.
   131→ *
   132→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph, then sets (evaluates) the expression immediately.
   133→ * Supports both binary and unary operator expressions.
   134→ *
   135→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   136→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   137→ * @tparam OpExpr The operator expression type (binary or unary).
   138→ * @param opExpr The operator expression to wrap.
   139→ * @return React<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   140→ */
   141→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsOpExpr OpExpr>
   142→auto expr(OpExpr &&opExpr) {
   143→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   144→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<OpExpr>(opExpr));

   147→    return React{ptr};

   156→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   157→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   158→ * @tparam Args Argument types for the callable.
   159→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   160→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   161→ * @return React<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   162→ */
   163→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   164→auto calc(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   165→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   166→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR>>();
   167→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   168→    ptr->set(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   169→    return React{ptr};

   172→/**
   173→ * @brief Alias for calc(), used to create a reactive action.
   174→ *
   175→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   176→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   177→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   178→ * @tparam Args Argument types.
   179→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   180→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   181→ * @return The reactive action wrapper.
   182→ */
   183→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   184→auto action(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   185→    return calc<TR, IV>(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);

   188→/**
   189→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive wrapper from a value or expression.
   190→ *
   191→ * If the input is a binary operator expression, creates an expr().
   192→ * If the input is an invocable callable, creates a calc().
   193→ * Otherwise, creates a var().
   194→ *
   195→ * @tparam T The type of input.
   196→ * @param t The input value, expression, or callable.
   197→ * @return Corresponding reactive wrapper.
   198→ */
   199→template <NonReact T>
   200→auto create(T &&t) {
   201→    if constexpr (IsBinaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>) {
   202→        return expr(std::forward<T>(t));
   203→    } else if constexpr (InvocableType<T>) {
   204→        return calc(std::forward<T>(t));
   205→    } else {
   206→        return var(std::forward<T>(t));
   207→    }
   208→}
   209→
   210→/**
   211→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive calculation from a callable and arguments.
   212→ *
   213→ * This function wraps a callable and its arguments into a reactive calculation,
   214→ * which automatically updates when any of its dependencies change.
   215→ *
   216→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   217→ * @tparam Args Argument types to be forwarded to the callable.
   218→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   219→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   220→ * @return A reactive calculation wrapper.
   221→ */
   222→template <typename Fun, typename... Args>
   223→auto create(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   224→    return calc(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   225→}

   227→/**
   228→ * @brief Begins a batch of reactive updates.
   229→ *
   230→ * This function creates a batch context, deferring propagation of reactive updates
   231→ * until the batch is executed. Useful for grouping multiple changes together efficiently.
   232→ *
   233→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   234→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations.
   235→ * @return A Batch object encapsulating the operation.
   236→ */
   237→template <InvocableType Fun>
   238→auto batch(Fun &&fun) {
   239→    return Batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   240→}
   241→
   242→/**
   243→ * @brief Immediately executes a batch of reactive updates.
   244→ *
   245→ * This function creates a batch context and executes it immediately.
   246→ * Any reactive updates are postponed until the end of the batch execution.
   247→ *
   248→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   249→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations to be executed.
   250→ */
   251→template <InvocableType Fun>
   252→void batchExecute(Fun &&fun) {
   253→    Batch batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   254→    batch.execute();
   255→}

   257→} // namespace reaction

    51→class FieldBase {

    55→     *

    67→    auto field(T &&t) {

    70→        FieldGraph::getInstance().addObj(m_id, ptr->shared_from_this());

    72→    }
    73→
    74→    /**
    75→     * @brief Get the unique identifier of this field base.
    76→     *
    77→     * @return uint64_t The unique ID.
    78→     */
    79→    uint64_t getId() {

    87→/**

    91→ * The reactive node is registered to the ObserverGraph.
    92→ *

    94→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    95→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
    96→ * @param t The value to wrap as a const reactive variable.
    97→ * @return React<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive constant wrapper.
    98→ */
    99→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   100→auto constVar(SrcType &&t) {
   101→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));

   107→ * @brief Create a reactive variable wrapping the given value.

   111→ *
   112→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   113→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   114→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
   115→ * @param t The value to wrap reactively.
   116→ * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive variable wrapper.
   117→ */
   118→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   119→auto var(SrcType &&t) {

   137→ * @tparam OpExpr The operator expression type (binary or unary).
   138→ * @param opExpr The operator expression to wrap.
   139→ * @return React<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   140→ */
   141→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsOpExpr OpExpr>
   142→auto expr(OpExpr &&opExpr) {
   143→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();

   147→    return React{ptr};

   156→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.

   158→ * @tparam Args Argument types for the callable.
   159→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   160→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   161→ * @return React<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   162→ */
   163→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   164→auto calc(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   165→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();

   170→}

   172→/**

   174→ *
   175→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   176→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   177→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   178→ * @tparam Args Argument types.
   179→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   180→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   181→ * @return The reactive action wrapper.
   182→ */
   183→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   184→auto action(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {

   188→/**

   192→ * If the input is an invocable callable, creates a calc().

   199→template <NonReact T>

   222→template <typename Fun, typename... Args>

   237→template <InvocableType Fun>

    47→struct WeakPtrHash {

     8→/**
     9→ * @file basic_example.cpp
    10→ * @brief Basic usage example of the Reaction framework
    11→ *
    12→ * This example demonstrates:
    13→ * - Creating reactive variables with var()
    14→ * - Computing derived values with calc() and expr()
    15→ * - Setting up reactive actions that respond to changes
    16→ * - Basic reactive dataflow patterns
    17→ *
    18→ * Use case: Stock price tracking with automatic profit/loss calculation
    19→ */
    20→
    21→#include <cmath>
    22→#include <iomanip>
    23→#include <iostream>
    24→#include <reaction/reaction.h>
    25→
    26→int main() {
    27→    using namespace reaction;
    28→
    29→    // === Step 1: Create reactive variables for stock prices ===
    30→    auto buyPrice = var(100.0).setName("buyPrice"); // Price at which stock was bought
    31→    auto currentPrice = var(105.0);                 // Current market price
    32→
    33→    // === Step 2: Compute profit/loss amount using calc() ===
    34→    // calc() creates a reactive calculation that automatically updates
    35→    // when its dependencies (buyPrice, currentPrice) change
    36→    auto profit = calc([&]() {
    37→        return currentPrice() - buyPrice();
    38→    });
    39→
    40→    // === Step 3: Compute percentage gain/loss using expr() ===
    41→    // expr() creates a reactive expression from operator overloads
    42→    // This demonstrates the mathematical expression syntax
    43→    auto profitPercent = expr(std::abs(currentPrice - buyPrice) / buyPrice * 100);
    44→
    45→    // === Step 4: Set up reactive logging with action() ===
    46→    // action() creates a side-effect that triggers when dependencies change
    47→    // This will automatically print updates whenever prices change
    48→    auto logger = action([&]() {
    49→        std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(2);
    50→        std::cout << "[Stock Update] Current Price: $" << currentPrice()
    51→                  << ", Profit: $" << profit()
    52→                  << " (" << profitPercent() << "%)\n";
    53→    });
    54→
    55→    // === Step 5: Simulate price changes ===
    56→    // Watch how all dependent calculations update automatically
    57→    currentPrice.value(110.0).value(95.0); // Stock price changes (chained updates)
    58→    buyPrice.value(90.0);                  // Buy price adjusted
    59→
    60→    return 0;
    61→}

    17→namespace reaction {
    18→
    19→/**
    20→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive variable (Var) based on VarExpr expression type.
    21→ *
    22→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type held by this reactive variable.
    23→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    24→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    25→ */
    26→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    27→using Var = React<VarExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    28→
    29→/**
    30→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive expression (Expr) based on BinaryOpExpr expression type.
    31→ *
    32→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type produced by this reactive calculation.
    33→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    34→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    35→ */
    36→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    37→using Calc = React<CalcExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    38→
    39→/**
    40→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive action (Action) based on CalcExpr expression type.
    41→ *
    42→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    43→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    44→ */
    45→template <IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    46→using Action = React<CalcExpr, Void, IV, TR>;
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * @brief Base class representing a field container in the reactive graph.
    50→ */
    51→class FieldBase {
    52→public:
    53→    /**
    54→     * @brief Create a reactive field from the provided initial value.
    55→     *
    56→     * This function creates a shared pointer to a ReactImpl representing
    57→     * a variable expression holding the given value. It registers the node
    58→     * to both the global ObserverGraph and FieldGraph using this FieldBase's ID.
    59→     *
    60→     * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    61→     * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    62→     * @tparam T The type of the initial value (deduced).
    63→     * @param t The initial value to store in the field.
    64→     * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR> A reactive wrapper around the stored value.
    65→     */
    66→    template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact T>
    67→    auto field(T &&t) {
    68→        auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<T>(t));
    69→        ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr->shared_from_this());
    70→        FieldGraph::getInstance().addObj(m_id, ptr->shared_from_this());
    71→        return React{ptr};
    72→    }
    73→
    74→    /**
    75→     * @brief Get the unique identifier of this field base.
    76→     *
    77→     * @return uint64_t The unique ID.
    78→     */
    79→    uint64_t getId() {
    80→        return m_id;
    81→    }
    82→
    83→private:
    84→    UniqueID m_id; ///< Unique identifier for this field instance.
    85→};
    86→
    87→/**
    88→ * @brief Create a constant reactive variable wrapping the given value.
    89→ *
    90→ * This is similar to var(), but the wrapped value is const.
    91→ * The reactive node is registered to the ObserverGraph.
    92→ *
    93→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    94→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    95→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
    96→ * @param t The value to wrap as a const reactive variable.
    97→ * @return React<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive constant wrapper.
    98→ */
    99→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   100→auto constVar(SrcType &&t) {
   101→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   102→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   103→    return React{ptr};
   104→}
   105→
   106→/**
   107→ * @brief Create a reactive variable wrapping the given value.
   108→ *
   109→ * If the source type supports the Field concept, binds the field in the FieldGraph.
   110→ * Registers the reactive node to the ObserverGraph.
   111→ *
   112→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   113→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   114→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
   115→ * @param t The value to wrap reactively.
   116→ * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive variable wrapper.
   117→ */
   118→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   119→auto var(SrcType &&t) {
   120→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   121→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   122→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   123→    if constexpr (HasField<SrcType>) {
   124→        FieldGraph::getInstance().bindField(t.getId(), ptr->shared_from_this());
   125→    }
   126→    return React{ptr};
   127→}
   128→
   129→/**
   130→ * @brief Create a reactive expression wrapping the given operator expression.
   131→ *
   132→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph, then sets (evaluates) the expression immediately.
   133→ * Supports both binary and unary operator expressions.
   134→ *
   135→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   136→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   137→ * @tparam OpExpr The operator expression type (binary or unary).
   138→ * @param opExpr The operator expression to wrap.
   139→ * @return React<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   140→ */
   141→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsOpExpr OpExpr>
   142→auto expr(OpExpr &&opExpr) {
   143→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   144→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<OpExpr>(opExpr));
   145→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   146→    ptr->set();
   147→    return React{ptr};
   148→}
   149→
   150→/**
   151→ * @brief Create a reactive calculation based on a callable and its arguments.
   152→ *
   153→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph and immediately sets (evaluates) the calculation.
   154→ *
   155→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   156→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   157→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   158→ * @tparam Args Argument types for the callable.
   159→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   160→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   161→ * @return React<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   162→ */
   163→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   164→auto calc(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {

     7→
     8→/**
     9→ * @file basic_example.cpp
    10→ * @brief Basic usage example of the Reaction framework
    11→ *
    12→ * This example demonstrates:
    13→ * - Creating reactive variables with var()
    14→ * - Computing derived values with calc() and expr()
    15→ * - Setting up reactive actions that respond to changes
    16→ * - Basic reactive dataflow patterns
    17→ *
    18→ * Use case: Stock price tracking with automatic profit/loss calculation
    19→ */
    20→
    21→#include <cmath>
    22→#include <iomanip>
    23→#include <iostream>
    24→#include <reaction/reaction.h>
    25→
    26→int main() {
    27→    using namespace reaction;
    28→
    29→    // === Step 1: Create reactive variables for stock prices ===
    30→    auto buyPrice = var(100.0).setName("buyPrice"); // Price at which stock was bought
    31→    auto currentPrice = var(105.0);                 // Current market price
    32→
    33→    // === Step 2: Compute profit/loss amount using calc() ===
    34→    // calc() creates a reactive calculation that automatically updates
    35→    // when its dependencies (buyPrice, currentPrice) change
    36→    auto profit = calc([&]() {
    37→        return currentPrice() - buyPrice();
    38→    });
    39→
    40→    // === Step 3: Compute percentage gain/loss using expr() ===
    41→    // expr() creates a reactive expression from operator overloads
    42→    // This demonstrates the mathematical expression syntax
    43→    auto profitPercent = expr(std::abs(currentPrice - buyPrice) / buyPrice * 100);
    44→
    45→    // === Step 4: Set up reactive logging with action() ===
    46→    // action() creates a side-effect that triggers when dependencies change
    47→    // This will automatically print updates whenever prices change
    48→    auto logger = action([&]() {
    49→        std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(2);
    50→        std::cout << "[Stock Update] Current Price: $" << currentPrice()
    51→                  << ", Profit: $" << profit()
    52→                  << " (" << profitPercent() << "%)\n";
    53→    });
    54→
    55→    // === Step 5: Simulate price changes ===
    56→    // Watch how all dependent calculations update automatically
    57→    currentPrice.value(110.0).value(95.0); // Stock price changes (chained updates)
    58→    buyPrice.value(90.0);                  // Buy price adjusted
    59→
    60→    return 0;
    61→}

    11→#include <utility>
    12→#include "reaction/core/id_generator.h"
    13→#include "reaction/core/react.h"
    14→#include "reaction/graph/field_graph.h"
    15→#include "reaction/graph/observer_graph.h"
    16→
    17→namespace reaction {
    18→
    19→/**
    20→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive variable (Var) based on VarExpr expression type.
    21→ *
    22→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type held by this reactive variable.
    23→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    24→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    25→ */
    26→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    27→using Var = React<VarExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    28→
    29→/**
    30→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive expression (Expr) based on BinaryOpExpr expression type.
    31→ *
    32→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type produced by this reactive calculation.
    33→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    34→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    35→ */
    36→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    37→using Calc = React<CalcExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    38→
    39→/**
    40→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive action (Action) based on CalcExpr expression type.
    41→ *
    42→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    43→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    44→ */
    45→template <IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    46→using Action = React<CalcExpr, Void, IV, TR>;
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * @brief Base class representing a field container in the reactive graph.
    50→ */
    51→class FieldBase {
    52→public:
    53→    /**
    54→     * @brief Create a reactive field from the provided initial value.
    55→     *
    56→     * This function creates a shared pointer to a ReactImpl representing
    57→     * a variable expression holding the given value. It registers the node
    58→     * to both the global ObserverGraph and FieldGraph using this FieldBase's ID.
    59→     *
    60→     * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    61→     * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    62→     * @tparam T The type of the initial value (deduced).
    63→     * @param t The initial value to store in the field.
    64→     * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR> A reactive wrapper around the stored value.
    65→     */
    66→    template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact T>
    67→    auto field(T &&t) {
    68→        auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<T>(t));
    69→        ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr->shared_from_this());
    70→        FieldGraph::getInstance().addObj(m_id, ptr->shared_from_this());
    71→        return React{ptr};
    72→    }
    73→
    74→    /**
    75→     * @brief Get the unique identifier of this field base.
    76→     *
    77→     * @return uint64_t The unique ID.
    78→     */
    79→    uint64_t getId() {
    80→        return m_id;
    81→    }
    82→
    83→private:
    84→    UniqueID m_id; ///< Unique identifier for this field instance.
    85→};
    86→
    87→/**
    88→ * @brief Create a constant reactive variable wrapping the given value.
    89→ *
    90→ * This is similar to var(), but the wrapped value is const.
    91→ * The reactive node is registered to the ObserverGraph.
    92→ *
    93→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    94→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    95→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
    96→ * @param t The value to wrap as a const reactive variable.
    97→ * @return React<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive constant wrapper.
    98→ */
    99→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   100→auto constVar(SrcType &&t) {
   101→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   102→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   103→    return React{ptr};
   104→}
   105→
   106→/**
   107→ * @brief Create a reactive variable wrapping the given value.
   108→ *
   109→ * If the source type supports the Field concept, binds the field in the FieldGraph.
   110→ * Registers the reactive node to the ObserverGraph.
   111→ *
   112→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   113→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   114→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
   115→ * @param t The value to wrap reactively.
   116→ * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive variable wrapper.
   117→ */
   118→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   119→auto var(SrcType &&t) {
   120→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   121→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   122→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   123→    if constexpr (HasField<SrcType>) {
   124→        FieldGraph::getInstance().bindField(t.getId(), ptr->shared_from_this());
   125→    }
   126→    return React{ptr};
   127→}
   128→
   129→/**
   130→ * @brief Create a reactive expression wrapping the given operator expression.
   131→ *
   132→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph, then sets (evaluates) the expression immediately.
   133→ * Supports both binary and unary operator expressions.
   134→ *
   135→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   136→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   137→ * @tparam OpExpr The operator expression type (binary or unary).
   138→ * @param opExpr The operator expression to wrap.
   139→ * @return React<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   140→ */
   141→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsOpExpr OpExpr>
   142→auto expr(OpExpr &&opExpr) {
   143→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   144→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<OpExpr>(opExpr));
   145→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   146→    ptr->set();
   147→    return React{ptr};
   148→}
   149→
   150→/**
   151→ * @brief Create a reactive calculation based on a callable and its arguments.
   152→ *
   153→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph and immediately sets (evaluates) the calculation.
   154→ *
   155→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   156→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   157→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   158→ * @tparam Args Argument types for the callable.
   159→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   160→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   161→ * @return React<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   162→ */
   163→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   164→auto calc(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   165→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   166→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR>>();
   167→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   168→    ptr->set(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   169→    return React{ptr};
   170→}
   171→
   172→/**
   173→ * @brief Alias for calc(), used to create a reactive action.
   174→ *
   175→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   176→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   177→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   178→ * @tparam Args Argument types.
   179→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   180→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   181→ * @return The reactive action wrapper.
   182→ */
   183→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   184→auto action(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   185→    return calc<TR, IV>(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   186→}
   187→
   188→/**
   189→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive wrapper from a value or expression.
   190→ *
   191→ * If the input is a binary operator expression, creates an expr().
   192→ * If the input is an invocable callable, creates a calc().
   193→ * Otherwise, creates a var().
   194→ *
   195→ * @tparam T The type of input.
   196→ * @param t The input value, expression, or callable.
   197→ * @return Corresponding reactive wrapper.
   198→ */
   199→template <NonReact T>
   200→auto create(T &&t) {
   201→    if constexpr (IsBinaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>) {
   202→        return expr(std::forward<T>(t));
   203→    } else if constexpr (InvocableType<T>) {
   204→        return calc(std::forward<T>(t));
   205→    } else {
   206→        return var(std::forward<T>(t));
   207→    }
   208→}
   209→
   210→/**
   211→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive calculation from a callable and arguments.
   212→ *
   213→ * This function wraps a callable and its arguments into a reactive calculation,
   214→ * which automatically updates when any of its dependencies change.
   215→ *
   216→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   217→ * @tparam Args Argument types to be forwarded to the callable.
   218→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   219→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   220→ * @return A reactive calculation wrapper.
   221→ */
   222→template <typename Fun, typename... Args>
   223→auto create(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   224→    return calc(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   225→}
   226→
   227→/**
   228→ * @brief Begins a batch of reactive updates.
   229→ *
   230→ * This function creates a batch context, deferring propagation of reactive updates
   231→ * until the batch is executed. Useful for grouping multiple changes together efficiently.
   232→ *
   233→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   234→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations.
   235→ * @return A Batch object encapsulating the operation.
   236→ */
   237→template <InvocableType Fun>
   238→auto batch(Fun &&fun) {
   239→    return Batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   240→}
   241→
   242→/**
   243→ * @brief Immediately executes a batch of reactive updates.
   244→ *
   245→ * This function creates a batch context and executes it immediately.
   246→ * Any reactive updates are postponed until the end of the batch execution.
   247→ *
   248→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   249→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations to be executed.
   250→ */
   251→template <InvocableType Fun>
   252→void batchExecute(Fun &&fun) {
   253→    Batch batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   254→    batch.execute();
   255→}

1→/*

     7→
     8→/**
     9→ * @file basic_example.cpp
    10→ * @brief Basic usage example of the Reaction framework
    11→ *
    12→ * This example demonstrates:
    13→ * - Creating reactive variables with var()
    14→ * - Computing derived values with calc() and expr()
    15→ * - Setting up reactive actions that respond to changes
    16→ * - Basic reactive dataflow patterns
    17→ *
    18→ * Use case: Stock price tracking with automatic profit/loss calculation
    19→ */
    20→
    21→#include <cmath>
    22→#include <iomanip>
    23→#include <iostream>
    24→#include <reaction/reaction.h>
    25→
    26→int main() {
    27→    using namespace reaction;
    28→
    29→    // === Step 1: Create reactive variables for stock prices ===
    30→    auto buyPrice = var(100.0).setName("buyPrice"); // Price at which stock was bought
    31→    auto currentPrice = var(105.0);                 // Current market price
    32→
    33→    // === Step 2: Compute profit/loss amount using calc() ===
    34→    // calc() creates a reactive calculation that automatically updates
    35→    // when its dependencies (buyPrice, currentPrice) change
    36→    auto profit = calc([&]() {
    37→        return currentPrice() - buyPrice();
    38→    });
    39→
    40→    // === Step 3: Compute percentage gain/loss using expr() ===
    41→    // expr() creates a reactive expression from operator overloads
    42→    // This demonstrates the mathematical expression syntax
    43→    auto profitPercent = expr(std::abs(currentPrice - buyPrice) / buyPrice * 100);
    44→
    45→    // === Step 4: Set up reactive logging with action() ===
    46→    // action() creates a side-effect that triggers when dependencies change
    47→    // This will automatically print updates whenever prices change
    48→    auto logger = action([&]() {
    49→        std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(2);
    50→        std::cout << "[Stock Update] Current Price: $" << currentPrice()
    51→                  << ", Profit: $" << profit()
    52→                  << " (" << profitPercent() << "%)\n";
    53→    });
    54→
    55→    // === Step 5: Simulate price changes ===
    56→    // Watch how all dependent calculations update automatically
    57→    currentPrice.value(110.0).value(95.0); // Stock price changes (chained updates)
    58→    buyPrice.value(90.0);                  // Buy price adjusted
    59→
    60→    return 0;
    61→}

     4→

    10→[![MVVM](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pattern-MVVM%2FMVC-9cf.svg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model–view–viewmodel)
    11→
    12→Reaction is a blazing-fast, modern C++20 header-only reactive framework that brings React/Vue-style dataflow to native C++ – perfect for **UI Dataflow**, **Game logic**, **Financial Services**, **Real-time calculation** and more.
    13→
    14→## 🚀 Performance Optimized
    15→
    16→- **Zero-cost abstractions** through compile-time calculation
    17→- Minimal runtime overhead with **smart change propagation**
    18→- Propagation efficiency **at the level of millions per second**
    19→
    20→## 🔗 Intelligent Dependency Management
    21→
    22→- Automatic **DAG detection** and cycle prevention
    23→- Fine-grained **change propagation control**
    24→- Optimize **multiple calls due to duplicate dependencies**
    25→
    26→## 🛡️ Safety Guarantees
    27→
    28→- Compile-time **type checking** with C++20 concepts
    29→- Safe **value semantics** throughout the framework
    30→- Framework manages node lifetime internally
    31→
    32→## 🔄 Multi-threading Support
    33→
    34→Reaction supports multi-threading with automatic thread safety detection and zero-overhead in single-threaded mode.
    35→
    36→---
    37→
    38→## 🔍 Comparison: `QProperty` vs `RxCpp` vs `Reaction`
    39→
    40→| Feature / Metric               | 🟩 **QProperty (Qt6)**                       | 🟨 **RxCpp**                                     | 🟥 **Reaction**                          |
    41→| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
    42→| **Expression Support**         | ✅ `setBinding()`, but only **single-layer**  | ✅ Supports chained `map`, `combine_latest`, etc. | ✅✅ Fully supports **deep nested expressions**                |
    43→| **Expression Nesting Depth**   | ❌ Limited to one layer                       | ⚠️ Supports nesting, but verbose                 | ✅ Unlimited depth with automatic dependency tracking         |
    44→| **Update Propagation**         | Manual propagation per layer                 | Reactive push chain per layer                    | Automatic DAG-based propagation with pruning                 |
    45→| **Dependency Tracking**        | ❌ Manual                                     | ⚠️ Manual via operator chaining                  | ✅ Automatic via lazy evaluation capturing dependencies       |
    46→| **Performance (Update Delay)** | ✅ Fast (O(1) propagation)                    | ❌ Slow (heap allocations and nested chaining)    | ✅✅ Fast (pruned update, lazy eval, diffing)                  |
    47→| **Memory Usage**               | ✅ Very low (stack + signals)                 | ❌ High (many heap-allocated observables)         | ⚠️ Moderate (DAG storage, optimized with small object opt.)  |
    48→| **Syntax Simplicity**          | ✅ Simple (`setBinding`, `value()`)           | ❌ Verbose template syntax                        | ✅ Clean expression templates, close to natural syntax        |
    49→| **Type Support**               | ✅ Built-ins and registered custom types      | ✅ Template-based, supports any type              | ✅ Type-erased or templated support for any combination       |
    50→| **Container Support**          | ✅ Can be used in containers                  | ✅ Can compose multiple observables               | ✅ Supports container expressions (e.g. map/filter outputs)   |
    51→| **Threading Model**            | UI-thread default, manual safety for signals | ✅ Multi-threaded pipelines                       | ✅ Main thread default, pluggable lock strategies             |
    52→| **Error Handling**             | ❌ None                                       | ✅ Robust error flow (`on_error_resume_next`)     | ✅ Error node propagation, pluggable failure strategy         |
    53→| **Debuggability**              | ⚠️ Lambdas harder to trace                   | ❌ Difficult due to complex types                 | ✅ Trackable dependencies, observable IDs, chain tracing      |
    54→| **Template Instance Size**     | ✅ Small                                      | ❌ Huge (template explosion)                      | ✅ Optimized with type-erasure or instance deduplication      |
    55→| **Build Time**                 | ✅ Fast                                       | ❌ Very slow for large expressions                | ✅ Separated headers, controllable instantiation              |
    56→| **Learning Curve**             | ✅ Low (Qt-style usage)                       | ❌ Steep (functional style)                       | ⚠️ Medium (understanding type deduction + expression design) |
    57→| **Use Case Fit**               | UI property binding, light state syncing     | Asynchronous pipelines, stream logic             | UI + state modeling + expression trees with complex logic    |

    81→### Key Findings:

    83→2. **Wide dependency scenarios**: ~2.76x faster than rxcpp, ~14.45x faster than folly

    98→## 🛠 Installation
    99→
   100→### 1. From source (manual installation)
   101→
   102→To build and install the `reaction` reactive framework manually:
   103→
   104→```bash
   105→git clone https://github.com/lumia431/reaction.git && cd reaction
   106→cmake -S . -B build
   107→cmake --install build/ --prefix /your/install/path
   108→```
   109→
   110→After installation, you can include and link against reaction in your own CMake-based project:
   111→
   112→```cmake
   113→find_package(reaction REQUIRED)

   115→```

   190→        std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(2);
   191→        std::cout << "[Stock Update] Current Price: $" << currentPrice()
   192→                  << ", Profit: $" << profit()
   193→                  << " (" << profitPercent() << "%)\n";
   194→    });
   195→
   196→    // Simulate price changes
   197→    currentPrice.value(110.0).value(95.0);  // Stock price increases
   198→    buyPrice.value(90.0);                   // Buy price adjusted
   199→
   200→    return 0;
   201→}
   202→```
   203→
   204→## 📖 Basic Usage
   205→
   206→### 1. Reactive Variables: `var`
   207→
   208→Define reactive state variables with `var<T>`.
   209→
   210→```cpp
   211→auto a = reaction::var(1);         // int variable
   212→auto b = reaction::var(3.14);      // double variable
   213→```
   214→
   215→- get value:
   216→
   217→```cpp
   218→auto val = a.get();
   219→```
   220→
   221→- assignment:
   222→
   223→```cpp
   224→a.value(2);
   225→```
   226→
   227→### 2. Derived Computation: calc
   228→
   229→Use **calc** to create reactive computations based on one or more var instances.
   230→
   231→- Lambda Capture Style:
   232→
   233→```cpp
   234→auto a = reaction::var(1);
   235→auto b = reaction::var(3.14);
   236→auto sum = reaction::calc([=]() {
   237→    return a() + b();  // Retrieve current values using a() and b()
   238→});
   239→```
   240→
   241→- Parameter Binding Style (High Performance):
   242→
   243→```cpp
   244→auto ds = reaction::calc([](auto aa, auto bb) {
   245→    return std::to_string(aa) + std::to_string(bb);
   246→}, a, b);  // Dependencies: a and b
   247→```
   248→
   249→### 3. Declarative Expression: expr
   250→
   251→expr provides a clean and concise syntax to declare reactive expressions. The result automatically updates when any dependent variable changes.
   252→
   253→```cpp
   254→auto a = reaction::var(1);
   255→auto b = reaction::var(2);
   256→auto result = reaction::expr(a + b * 3);  // result updates automatically when 'a' or 'b' change
   257→```
   258→
   259→### 4. Reactive Side Effects: action
   260→
   261→Register actions to perform side effects whenever the observed variables change.
   262→
   263→```cpp
   264→int val = 10;
   265→auto a = reaction::var(1);
   266→auto dds = reaction::action([&val]() {
   267→    val = a();
   268→});
   269→```
   270→
   271→Ofcourse, to get high performance can use Parameter Binding Style.
   272→
   273→```cpp
   274→int val = 10;
   275→auto a = reaction::var(1);
   276→auto dds = reaction::action([&val](auto aa) {
   277→    val = aa;
   278→}, a);
   279→```
   280→
   281→### 5. Reactive Struct Fields
   282→
   283→For complex types with reactive fields allow you to define struct-like variables whose members are individually reactive.
   284→
   285→Here's an example of a `PersonField` class:
   286→
   287→```cpp
   288→class PersonField : public reaction::FieldBase {
   289→public:
   290→    PersonField(std::string name, int age):
   291→        m_name(reaction::field(name)),
   292→        m_age(reaction::field(age)){}
   293→
   294→    std::string getName() const { return m_name.get(); }
   295→    void setName(const std::string &name) { m_name.value(name); }
   296→    int getAge() const { return m_age.get(); }
   297→    void setAge(int age) { m_age.value(age); }
   298→
   299→private:
   300→    reaction::Var<std::string> m_name;
   301→    reaction::Var<int> m_age;
   302→};
   303→
   304→auto p = reaction::var(PersonField{"Jack", 18});
   305→auto action = reaction::action(
   306→    []() {
   307→        std::cout << "Action Trigger , name = " << p().getName() << " age = " << p().getAge() << '\n';
   308→    });
   309→
   310→p->setName("Jackson"); // Action Trigger
   311→p->setAge(28);         // Action Trigger
   312→```
   313→
   314→### 6. Copy and move semantics support
   315→
   316→```cpp
   317→auto a = reaction::var(1);
   318→auto b = reaction::var(3.14);
   319→auto ds = reaction::calc([]() { return a() + b(); });
   320→auto ds_copy = ds;
   321→auto ds_move = std::move(ds);
   322→EXPECT_FALSE(static_cast<bool>(ds));
   323→```
   324→
   325→### 7. Resetting Nodes and Dependencies
   326→
   327→The reaction framework allows you to **reset a computation node** by replacing its computation function.
   328→This mechanism is useful when the result needs to be recalculated using a different logic or different dependencies after the node has been initially created.
   329→
   330→``Note:`` **The return value type cannot be changed**
   331→
   332→Below is an example that demonstrates the reset functionality:
   333→
   334→```cpp
   335→TEST(TestReset, ReactionTest) {
   336→    auto a = reaction::var(1);
   337→    auto b = reaction::var(std::string{"2"});
   338→    auto ds = reaction::calc([]() { return std::to_string(a()); });
   339→    ds.reset([=]() { return b() + "set"; });
   340→
   341→    v.value("3");
   342→    EXPECT_EQ(ds.get(), "3set");
   343→
   344→    EXPECT_THROW(ds.reset([=]() { return a(); }), std::runtime_error);  // return type changed
   345→    EXPECT_THROW(ds.reset([=]() { return ds(); }), std::runtime_error); // cycle dependent
   346→}
   347→```
   348→
   349→### 8. Trigger Mode
   350→
   351→The `reaction` framework supports various triggering mode to control when reactive computations are re-evaluated. This example demonstrates three mode:
   352→
   353→1. **Value Change Trigger:** The reactive computation is triggered only when the underlying value actually changes.
   354→2. **Filter Trigger:** The reactive computation is triggered when the value crosses a specified condition.
   355→3. **Always Trigger:** (Not explicitly shown in this example) Always triggers regardless of whether the value has changed.
   356→
   357→The trigger Mode can be specified by the type parameter
   358→
   359→```cpp
   360→using namespace reaction;
   361→auto stockPrice = var(100.0);
   362→auto profit = expr(stockPrice() - 100.0);   // defalut ChangeTrigger
   363→auto assignAction = action<AlwaysTrig>([=]() {
   364→    std::cout << "Checky assign, price = " << stockPrice() <<'\n';
   365→});
   366→auto sellAction = action<FilterTrig>([=]() {
   367→    std::cout << "It's time to sell, profit = " << profit() <<'\n';
   368→});
   369→sellAction.filter([=]() {
   370→    return profit() > 5.0;
   371→});
   372→stockPrice.value(100.0); // assignAction trigger
   373→stockPrice.value(101.0); // assignAction, profit trigger
   374→stockPrice.value(106.0); // all trigger
   375→
   376→```
   377→
   378→You can even define a trigger mode yourself in your code, just include the **checkTrig** method:
   379→
   380→```cpp
   381→struct MyTrig {
   382→    bool checkTrig() {
   383→        // do something
   384→        return true;
   385→    }
   386→};
   387→auto a = var(1);
   388→auto b = expr<MyTrig>(a + 1);
   389→```
   390→
   391→### 9. Invalid Handles
   392→
   393→In the `reaction` framework, all data sources **obtained by users are actually in the form of weak references**, and their actual memory is managed **in the observer map**.
   394→Users can manually call the **close** method, so that all dependent data sources will also be closed.
   395→
   396→```cpp
   397→auto a = reaction::var(1);
   398→auto b = reaction::var(2);
   399→auto dsA = reaction::calc([=]() { return a(); });
   400→auto dsB = reaction::calc([=]() { return dsA() + b(); });
   401→dsA.close(); //dsB will automatically close, cause dsB dependents dsA.
   402→EXPECT_FALSE(static_cast<bool>(dsA));
   403→EXPECT_FALSE(static_cast<bool>(dsB));
   404→```
   405→
   406→However, for scenarios where the lifecycle of a weak reference acquired by user ends, the `reaction` framework makes several strategy for different scenarios.
   407→
   408→- **CloseHandle:**
   409→  The node is immediately closed (made invalid) when any of its dependencies become invalid.
   410→
   411→- **KeepHandle:**
   412→  The node continues to recalculate, its dependencies work normally.
   413→
   414→- **LastHandle:**
   415→  The node retains the last valid, its dependencies use the value to calculate.
   416→
   417→Below is a concise example that illustrates all three strategies:
   418→
   419→```cpp
   420→{
   421→    auto a = var(1);
   422→    auto b = calc([]() { return a(); });
   423→    {
   424→        auto temp = calc<AlwaysTrig, CloseHandle>([]() { return a(); });
   425→        b.set([](auto t) { return t; }, temp);
   426→    }
   427→    // temp lifecycle ends, b will end too.
   428→    EXPECT_FALSE(static_cast<bool>(b));
   429→}
   430→{
   431→    auto a = var(1);
   432→    auto b = calc([]() { return a(); });
   433→    {
   434→        auto temp = calc<AlwaysTrig, KeepHandle>([]() { return a(); }); // default is KeepHandle
   435→        b.set([](auto t) { return t; }, temp);
   436→    }
   437→    // temp lifecycle ends, b not be influenced.
   438→    EXPECT_TRUE(static_cast<bool>(b));
   439→    EXPECT_EQ(b.get(), 1);
   440→    a.value(2);
   441→    EXPECT_EQ(b.get(), 2);
   442→}
   443→{
   444→    auto a = var(1);
   445→    auto b = calc([]() { return a(); });
   446→    {
   447→        auto temp = calc<AlwaysTrig, LastHandle>([]() { return a(); });
   448→        b.set([](auto t) { return t; }, temp);
   449→    }
   450→    // temp lifecycle ends, b use its last val to calculate.
   451→    EXPECT_TRUE(static_cast<bool>(b));
   452→    EXPECT_EQ(b.get(), 1);
   453→    a.value(2);
   454→    EXPECT_EQ(b.get(), 1);
   455→}
   456→```
   457→
   458→Likewise, you can define a strategy yourself in your code, just include the **handleInvalid** method:
   459→
   460→```cpp
   461→struct MyHandle {
   462→    void handleInvalid() {
   463→        std::cout << "Invalid" << std::endl;
   464→    }
   465→};
   466→auto a = var(1);
   467→auto b = expr<AlwaysTrig, MyHandle>(a + 1);
   468→```
   469→
   470→### 10. Reactive Containers
   471→
   472→**Reaction** supports reactive versions of standard stl containers (`vector, list, set, map`, etc.).
   473→
   474→```cpp
   475→
   476→using namespace reaction;
   477→constexpr int STUDENT_COUNT = 5;
   478→// 1. Student grades container - using vector to store VarExpr
   479→std::vector<Var<double>> grades;
   480→for (int i = 0; i < STUDENT_COUNT; ++i) {
   481→    grades.push_back(create(70.0 + i * 5));
   482→}
   483→// 2. Grade statistics container - using list to store CalcExpr
   484→std::list<Calc<double>> stats;
   485→stats.push_back(create([&] {
   486→    double sum = 0;
   487→    for (auto &grade : grades)
   488→        sum += grade();
   489→    return sum / grades.size();
   490→}));
   491→stats.push_back(create([&] {
   492→    double max = grades[0].get();
   493→    for (auto &grade : grades)
   494→        max = std::max(max, grade());
   495→    return max;
   496→}));
   497→// 3. Grade change monitors - using set to store Action
   498→std::set<Action<>> monitors;
   499→for (int i = 0; i < STUDENT_COUNT; ++i) {
   500→    monitors.insert(create([i, &grades] {
   501→        std::cout << "[Monitor] Student " << i << " grade updated: " << grades[i]() << "\n";
   502→    }));
   503→}
   504→// 4. Grade level mapping - using map to store CalcExpr
   505→std::map<int, Calc<const char *>> gradeLevels;
   506→for (int i = 0; i < STUDENT_COUNT; ++i) {
   507→    gradeLevels.insert({i, create([i, &grades] {
   508→                            double g = grades[i]();
   509→                            if (g >= 90) return "A";
   510→                            if (g >= 80) return "B";
   511→                            if (g >= 70) return "C";
   512→                            return "D";
   513→                        })});
   514→}
   515→
   516→```
   517→
   518→### 11. Batch Operations
   519→
   520→**Reaction** allows grouping multiple reactive updates into a single **batch**, deferring propagation until the batch ends.
   521→This helps eliminate redundant intermediate updates and improves performance when updating multiple reactive nodes at once.
   522→
   523→```cpp
   524→using namespace reaction;
   525→
   526→Var<int> a = create(1);
   527→Var<int> b = create(2);
   528→
   529→// Create a computed value depending on both a and b
   530→Calc<int> sum = create([&] {
   531→    std::cout << "[Recompute] sum = " << a() << " + " << b() << "\n";
   532→    return a() + b();
   533→});
   534→
   535→// 1. Without batching: triggers recomputation twice
   536→a.value(10);  // [Recompute] sum = 10 + 2
   537→b.value(20);  // [Recompute] sum = 10 + 20
   538→
   539→// 2. With batching: triggers recomputation only once
   540→auto batchScope = batch([&] {
   541→    a.value(100);
   542→    b.value(200);
   543→});
   544→batchScope.execute();       // [Recompute] sum = 100 + 200
   545→
   546→// or you can use 'batchExecute' to execute directly
   547→batchExecute([&] {
   548→    a.value(300);
   549→    b.value(400);
   550→});                         // [Recompute] sum = 300 + 400
   551→```
   552→

    17→namespace reaction {
    18→
    19→/**
    20→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive variable (Var) based on VarExpr expression type.
    21→ *
    22→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type held by this reactive variable.
    23→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    24→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    25→ */
    26→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    27→using Var = React<VarExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    28→
    29→/**
    30→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive expression (Expr) based on BinaryOpExpr expression type.
    31→ *
    32→ * @tparam SrcType The underlying data type produced by this reactive calculation.
    33→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    34→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    35→ */
    36→template <NonReact SrcType, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    37→using Calc = React<CalcExpr, SrcType, IV, TR>;
    38→
    39→/**
    40→ * @brief Alias template for a reactive action (Action) based on CalcExpr expression type.
    41→ *
    42→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    43→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    44→ */
    45→template <IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig>
    46→using Action = React<CalcExpr, Void, IV, TR>;
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * @brief Base class representing a field container in the reactive graph.
    50→ */
    51→class FieldBase {
    52→public:
    53→    /**
    54→     * @brief Create a reactive field from the provided initial value.
    55→     *
    56→     * This function creates a shared pointer to a ReactImpl representing
    57→     * a variable expression holding the given value. It registers the node
    58→     * to both the global ObserverGraph and FieldGraph using this FieldBase's ID.
    59→     *
    60→     * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    61→     * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    62→     * @tparam T The type of the initial value (deduced).
    63→     * @param t The initial value to store in the field.
    64→     * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR> A reactive wrapper around the stored value.
    65→     */
    66→    template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact T>
    67→    auto field(T &&t) {
    68→        auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<T>(t));
    69→        ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr->shared_from_this());
    70→        FieldGraph::getInstance().addObj(m_id, ptr->shared_from_this());
    71→        return React{ptr};
    72→    }
    73→
    74→    /**
    75→     * @brief Get the unique identifier of this field base.
    76→     *
    77→     * @return uint64_t The unique ID.
    78→     */
    79→    uint64_t getId() {
    80→        return m_id;
    81→    }
    82→
    83→private:
    84→    UniqueID m_id; ///< Unique identifier for this field instance.
    85→};
    86→
    87→/**
    88→ * @brief Create a constant reactive variable wrapping the given value.
    89→ *
    90→ * This is similar to var(), but the wrapped value is const.
    91→ * The reactive node is registered to the ObserverGraph.
    92→ *
    93→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    94→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    95→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
    96→ * @param t The value to wrap as a const reactive variable.
    97→ * @return React<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive constant wrapper.
    98→ */
    99→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   100→auto constVar(SrcType &&t) {
   101→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   102→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   103→    return React{ptr};
   104→}
   105→
   106→/**
   107→ * @brief Create a reactive variable wrapping the given value.
   108→ *
   109→ * If the source type supports the Field concept, binds the field in the FieldGraph.
   110→ * Registers the reactive node to the ObserverGraph.
   111→ *
   112→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   113→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   114→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
   115→ * @param t The value to wrap reactively.
   116→ * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive variable wrapper.
   117→ */
   118→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   119→auto var(SrcType &&t) {
   120→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   121→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   122→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   123→    if constexpr (HasField<SrcType>) {
   124→        FieldGraph::getInstance().bindField(t.getId(), ptr->shared_from_this());
   125→    }
   126→    return React{ptr};
   127→}
   128→
   129→/**
   130→ * @brief Create a reactive expression wrapping the given operator expression.
   131→ *
   132→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph, then sets (evaluates) the expression immediately.
   133→ * Supports both binary and unary operator expressions.
   134→ *
   135→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   136→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   137→ * @tparam OpExpr The operator expression type (binary or unary).
   138→ * @param opExpr The operator expression to wrap.
   139→ * @return React<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   140→ */
   141→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsOpExpr OpExpr>
   142→auto expr(OpExpr &&opExpr) {
   143→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   144→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<OpExpr>(opExpr));
   145→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   146→    ptr->set();
   147→    return React{ptr};
   148→}
   149→
   150→/**
   151→ * @brief Create a reactive calculation based on a callable and its arguments.
   152→ *
   153→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph and immediately sets (evaluates) the calculation.
   154→ *
   155→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   156→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   157→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   158→ * @tparam Args Argument types for the callable.
   159→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   160→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   161→ * @return React<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   162→ */
   163→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   164→auto calc(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   165→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   166→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR>>();
   167→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   168→    ptr->set(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   169→    return React{ptr};
   170→}
   171→
   172→/**
   173→ * @brief Alias for calc(), used to create a reactive action.
   174→ *
   175→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   176→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   177→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   178→ * @tparam Args Argument types.
   179→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   180→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   181→ * @return The reactive action wrapper.
   182→ */
   183→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   184→auto action(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   185→    return calc<TR, IV>(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   186→}
   187→
   188→/**
   189→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive wrapper from a value or expression.
   190→ *
   191→ * If the input is a binary operator expression, creates an expr().
   192→ * If the input is an invocable callable, creates a calc().
   193→ * Otherwise, creates a var().
   194→ *
   195→ * @tparam T The type of input.
   196→ * @param t The input value, expression, or callable.
   197→ * @return Corresponding reactive wrapper.
   198→ */
